readings: There is one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ
Even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs
2027-06-10.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), which began at Pentecost: the Church remembers how the apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, carried the Gospel to the nations. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and from Pentecost the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. Today's readings are taken from the official First Set calendar of 2022-23 (the Fourth Thursday of the Apostles), because in the 2024-25 calendar from which this month is mapped the same day was the Dukhrana of St Thomas; verify locally. In the Latin calendar, a weekday of the tenth week in Ordinary Time.
2027-06-10.verse: But she answered him, “Sir, even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
theo: Today the Gospel takes Jesus out of Galilee. Mark says that “he set out and went away to the region of Tyre”, a Gentile coastal region on the Mediterranean, in what is now southern Lebanon. He enters a house and wants no one to know he is there, perhaps seeking rest with his disciples. “Yet he could not escape notice.” A woman hears of him and comes at once, because her little daughter is tormented by an unclean spirit. Mark is careful to tell us who she is: “the woman was a Gentile, of Syrophoenician origin.” She is outside the people of the covenant, a woman, a foreigner, without any claim on a Jewish teacher. She bows down at his feet and begs him to cast the demon out of her daughter. Every parent who has prayed at night for a sick or troubled child knows what was in her heart.

Jesus' answer sounds hard to our ears: “Let the children be fed first, for it is not fair to take the children's food and throw it to the dogs.” We should not soften it too quickly, but we should read it well. Jesus speaks of an order in God's plan: the promises were made first to Israel, the children of the household, and the Messiah came first to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The word he uses can mean the little dogs of the house, not the wild dogs of the street. And the word “first” leaves a door open: if the children are fed first, then someone else is fed afterwards. The woman hears the open door and walks through it with faith and wit: “Sir, even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs.” She does not argue that she deserves the bread. She trusts that there is so much bread at this table that even the crumbs are enough for her daughter. She calls him “Sir”, or “Lord”, the only person in Mark's Gospel to address Jesus with that title. And Jesus answers, “For saying that, you may go; the demon has left your daughter.” She goes home and finds the child lying quietly on the bed, healed.

Mark places this story just after Jesus has declared all foods clean (Mark 7:19), and just before he feeds a crowd in Gentile territory (Mark 8:1–10). The bread of the children is about to overflow the table. In this Season of the Apostles the Church remembers how that happened: after the Resurrection and Pentecost the apostles carried the bread of the Gospel to the nations, and the household of God was opened to all. We, the Christians of India, are among those who were once outside the table. Through the apostle Thomas, as our tradition holds, the bread came to our shores. Every Holy Qurbana we celebrate is a sign that the Syrophoenician woman's hope was right: there is enough at the Lord's table for all.

Paul's letter speaks of a very practical question in Corinth: may Christians eat meat that has been offered in pagan temples? Some say, “all of us possess knowledge”: we know that idols are nothing, so we may eat anything. Paul agrees with the doctrine but corrects the attitude: “Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up. Anyone who claims to know something does not yet have the necessary knowledge; but anyone who loves God is known by him.” Then he proclaims the heart of the faith in words that sound like an early creed: “yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and for whom we exist, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and through whom we exist.” This is the Shema of Israel, “Hear, O Israel: The Lord is our God, the Lord alone” (Deuteronomy 6:4), opened up to include Jesus within the one God. We say the same in the Creed every Sunday. But Paul's point is that right doctrine must be held with love. The one who knows the truth must use it to build up the weak, not to show off or to wound.

Both readings meet in a single lesson. The proud knowledge of the Corinthians puffed them up; the humble faith of a foreign mother won her daughter's healing. It is not always the one who knows most who receives most, but the one who trusts most and loves most. Today let us pray for parents who carry a child's illness or struggle to the Lord; for those who feel they have no claim on God; and for ourselves, that our knowledge of the faith may become love that builds up.
outline: A foreign mother at the feet of Jesus in the region of Tyre.
Point 1 · She could not be kept away
A parent's love and a Gentile's faith.
Point 2 · Even the dogs eat the crumbs
Humble, persistent, witty trust; the table that is enough for all.
The creed of Israel opened to Christ.
Point 4 · Knowledge puffs up, love builds up
“Even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs.”
live: Name a child or young person you love who is struggling, and bring them to Jesus each day this week with persistent faith.
Build up, do not puff up (1 Corinthians 8:1)
In one conversation about faith this week, choose to encourage rather than to win the argument.
At the next Holy Qurbana, pray the Creed slowly and mean each phrase about the one God and the one Lord.
fathers: See the woman's wisdom: she does not contradict the Lord, nor is she grieved at being called a dog; she takes his very word and turns it into a plea. Her persistence is rewarded because it came from faith.
Christ seemed to reject her so that her humility might be revealed; she accepted the lowly name and so received the high gift. Humility opened what pride would have kept closed.
magis: Just as Jesus prays to the Father and gives thanks before receiving his gifts, he teaches us filial boldness: everything is possible for one who believes. Jesus is moved by the faith of those who ask, like the Canaanite woman.
Everyone is called to enter the kingdom. First announced to the children of Israel, this messianic kingdom is intended to accept people of all nations.
Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord: faith in God leads us to turn to him alone as our first origin and our ultimate goal.
saints: Fourth Thursday of the Apostles (readings from the First Set 2022-23 calendar). In the Latin calendar, a weekday of the tenth week in Ordinary Time.

7–12 June: the fourth week of the Season of the Apostles. Tue 8: St Mariam Thresia, the saint of the families of Kerala (an important feast). Wed 9: Mar Aprem, St Ephrem the Syrian, the Harp of the Spirit (an important feast; in the Latin calendar an optional memorial the same day). Thu 10: Fourth Thursday of the Apostles. Fri 11: St Barnabas, the Apostle (in the Latin calendar a memorial the same day). Sun 13: Fifth Sunday of the Apostles; St Antony of Padua, so dear to Kerala, gives way to the Sunday this year. June is the month of the Sacred Heart, and in Kerala the month of the monsoon and of the new school year.
2027-06-10.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you could not be hidden from the mother who came to you for her daughter, and you rejoiced in her humble and persistent faith. Look on the children we carry in our hearts: heal the sick, deliver those who are oppressed, and bring back those who have wandered. Teach us to trust that there is bread enough at your table for all. One God and Father, from whom are all things and for whom we exist, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we exist, keep us in the true faith and make our knowledge humble and our love strong, so that we may build up and not puff up. With the Holy Spirit be glory to you for ever. Amen.
altar: The Syrophoenician woman asked only for crumbs. At the Holy Qurbana the Lord gives us not crumbs but the Bread itself, his own Body and Blood, at a table opened to all nations. Let us come with her humility and her trust, and let us remember those who still wait outside.

quick: A Gentile mother from the region of Tyre begs Jesus to heal her daughter.
Her humble, persistent faith: even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs; and her daughter is healed.
Paul: knowledge puffs up, but love builds up; for us there is one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ.
2027-06-10.action: Pray each day this week, with persistent faith, for one young person who is struggling.
2027-06-10.question: Do I use what I know about the faith to build others up or to set myself above them?

family.explain: A mother who was not Jewish came to Jesus because her little girl was very ill. Jesus tested her faith by saying the children's bread was for the children first. She answered cleverly: even the little dogs under the table get the crumbs! She trusted that Jesus had so much love that even a little would be enough. Jesus was happy with her faith, and her daughter was healed. God's love is for everyone, from every country.
family.intention: We pray for children who are sick or troubled, and for mothers and fathers who pray for them.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we keep asking God for as a family? Let us not give up!”

illus: A mother in Kozhikode had a teenage son who had fallen into drugs. For two years she went to the adoration chapel near her parish every evening after work and stayed half an hour. Her friends told her gently that she should accept things as they were. She said only, ‘I am not asking for much. A crumb from his table is enough for my son.’ One night the boy, after a frightening episode with friends, walked into the same chapel looking for her. He sat beside her in silence. Months later, in a recovery programme, he told a counsellor that he had come back because he knew exactly where his mother would be, and that her stubborn prayer had been the only thing in his life that never changed.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you could not be hidden from those who seek you. We come to you as the Syrophoenician mother came, with our needs and our children. Give us her humble and persistent faith, and fill us with your Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: She bowed down at his feet (Mark 7:25). For whom am I bowing down before Jesus today?
Even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs (Mark 7:28). Do I trust that a little of God's grace is enough?
Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up (1 Corinthians 8:1). When has my knowledge made me proud?
One God, the Father… and one Lord, Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 8:6). What place does the Creed have in my daily life?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on our children.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that her table may be open to people of every nation.
For parents who pray for sick, troubled or wandering children, that their faith may not fail.
For young people caught in addiction, that they may be set loose from every evil spirit.
For theologians, teachers and catechists, that their knowledge may become love that builds up.
For migrants and foreigners among us, that they may find welcome at the Lord's table.
pm.close: Lord God, you rejoiced in the faith of a foreign mother and healed her daughter. Give us persistent faith, humble knowledge and love that builds up, and gather all nations at the table of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today Jesus goes to the region of Tyre, outside Israel. He wants to stay hidden, but a mother finds him. She is a Gentile, a foreigner, and her little daughter is tormented by an evil spirit. She falls at his feet and begs for help.

Jesus answers with words that sound hard: the children must be fed first; it is not fair to give the children's bread to the dogs. He is testing her, and he is speaking of God's plan, which began with Israel. But notice the word “first”: after the children, someone else will be fed.

The woman does not give up. She says: “Sir, even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs” (Mark 7:28). She does not claim that she deserves the bread. She only trusts that there is so much bread at the Lord's table that a crumb will be enough. Jesus rejoices in her faith, and her daughter is healed.

Saint Paul tells the Corinthians that “knowledge puffs up, but love builds up” (1 Corinthians 8:1). The clever Corinthians were proud of what they knew. The foreign mother knew little, but she trusted much and loved much. And Paul reminds us of our faith: there is one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ.

We too were once outside the table. Through the apostles, the Gospel reached our land. Now at every Holy Qurbana we receive not crumbs but the Bread of life itself. Let us pray with this mother's persistence for the children we love, and let us use what we know of the faith to build others up. Amen.
kids: Children, a mother came to Jesus because her little girl was sick. Jesus tested her, but she did not give up! She said that even a crumb from his table would be enough. Jesus was so happy with her faith that he healed her daughter. When you pray, do not give up. Keep asking Jesus with trust, because he loves you very much.
